value.title: PRD 006: seat types
value.summary: Every community role names one of ten types that says how its seat lives: what it is for, when it is compacted or closed, and what it must keep written down. Types are pij's fixed set; roles stay the open set each repo builds on top of them.

sections.name: why
sections.value: A pij community is meant to be a team of experts that learns a problem space nobody could map in advance, not only a way to run coders in parallel. Today pij cannot tell those seats apart. The daemon acts on four seat roles (`prime`, `pm`, `worker`, `pa`), and assigning any other community role stamps the seat `worker`, so a topic expert, a graph keeper and a coder look the same. A role's `kind` (`specialist` or `general`) carries no rules, and nearly every role is `specialist`. On 2026-11-24 the primes of five fleets were asked how they use their seats. All five asked for a named knowledge type, and they sorted their seats into the same few kinds without having words for them. The operator's rulings from that conversation: a coder or reviewer is compacted after every job because its size matters more than what it remembers; a knowledge seat is the expert, not the database, and is responsible for writing what it learns into graphs or markdown that can be read without it.

value.name: operator
value.need: Know what kind of seat each one is and trust that it is treated accordingly.

value.name: prime
value.need: Create a role by saying how it should live, without writing its lifecycle rules by hand each time.

value.name: role holder
value.need: Be told, at the start, what kind of seat it is and what that requires of it.

value.goal: pij can tell a coder from an expert from a human's window, for every seat that holds a role.
A repo builds any role it needs on a type, and never needs to change pij to do it.

value.text: Having the daemon enforce a type's rules, such as compacting a coder itself. This PRD states the rules and tells the seat; enforcement is later work.
Changing the large-seat alert, the idle nudge or which fleet messages may wake a seat.

Changing what a prime, a project manager or a PA is allowed to do, or any other permission rule (PRD 003). The `--role pm|worker|pa` flag on spawn and link keeps working; `worker` simply means no authority of its own.
Letting a repo define its own type.

value.title: Every role has one type
value.statement: A role names exactly one type from pij's set: `prime`, `pa`, `project-manager`, `coder`, `reviewer`, `worker`, `knowledge`, `steward`, `watcher` or `human-window`. `pij directory add` and `edit` take `--type`, and `add` refuses a role with no type, listing the ten with one line each.
value.done_when: `pij directory add x --why y` with no type or template refuses and prints the ten types; the same call with `--type knowledge` writes a role whose document shows that type.

value.title: Each type says what it means
value.statement: pij ships one short definition per type: what the seat is for, when it is compacted or closed, and what it must keep. A coder builds one step and is compacted after every job. A reviewer judges one piece of work at its exact version, independently of its author, and is compacted after every job unless its role keeps standing context, as security may. A worker does one other piece of work and is closed. A knowledge seat is the expert who owns one area and keeps what it learns written down. A steward is the only writer of one shared thing. A project manager runs a workstream and holds its history. A watcher reacts to events and rebuilds from current state. A human-window is one person's seat into the fleet. Prime and PA keep the duties they have today.
value.done_when: For each of the ten types, pij prints its definition on request, and a seat started in a role of that type receives it.
value.source: operator rulings 2026-11-25; interviews with five primes 2026-11-24

value.title: A type asks for what it needs
value.statement: Creating a role asks for what its type requires. A knowledge role names the artefact it keeps current (a graph or a file path). A steward role names the one thing it is sole writer of. `add` refuses when the required field is missing and names it.
value.done_when: `pij directory add x --type knowledge --why y` with no artefact refuses and names the missing field; with one, the role document records it.
value.source: operator ruling 2026-11-25: knowledge seats project what they know into static forms

value.title: A seat holds roles of one type
value.statement: The prime's view marks a seat that holds roles of two different types and proposes the split, since their rules conflict (a coder is compacted after each job; an expert is kept).
value.done_when: With one seat assigned a coder role and a knowledge role, `pij directory` lists it as an action naming both roles.

value.title: One label per seat, and three types carry authority
value.statement: A seat has one label, its type, shown by `pij directory` and `pij list`. Only three types carry authority of their own: prime, project manager and PA keep exactly the powers those seats have today. The other seven carry none, which is what `worker` means today, so there is no separate worker label to keep in step. Who may govern a particular seat still comes from its recorded parent and the prime designation.
value.done_when: A seat assigned a knowledge role and a seat assigned a coder role show different types in `pij list --json` and neither has any power a plain worker lacks; a prime, a project manager and a PA can do everything they could before; and every existing permission test still passes.
value.source: operator ruling 2026-11-25: just prime, pm and pa, simplify; code reading: every other role is stamped worker at assignment

value.title: Roles extend types; types are fixed
value.statement: A role inherits its type's rules and may add its own. A type marks each of its rules as fixed or as a default a role may change with a reason: a coder is always compacted after every job, while a reviewer role may keep standing context instead. A repo cannot add a type. When no type fits, the creator picks the nearest, puts the difference in the role's rules and records a type suggestion that the pij project can read.
value.done_when: A coder role edited to remove the compact-after-each-job rule is refused; a reviewer role created to keep standing context is accepted and its document records the reason; a recorded type suggestion appears in the view.
value.source: operator, 2026-11-25: dynamic roles come off one of our base types; security is a reviewer whose compaction is optional

value.title: Existing roles get a type
value.statement: One command gives every existing role a type, proposing one from the role's template and id and leaving the rest for the prime to choose. `kind` and `lifecycle` are retired, and a role document written before the change still reads.
value.done_when: Run on a community of roles written before this change, the command leaves no role without a type, lists each one it could not decide, and `pij directory` reads the result.
value.source: role documents in five projects use kind and lifecycle today

value.title: Every type ships a seed template a repo can change
value.statement: pij ships a seed template for each of the ten types: the text a seat of that type is told at start. The prime and project-manager seeds carry firm guidance on how to govern. The coder, reviewer, security and other seeds are working examples that a repo is encouraged to replace or extend for its own work. A repo edits its own copy of any of them, and a prime may change its own.
value.done_when: pij prints a seed for each of the ten types; a repo's edited copy of the coder seed is what a new coder there receives; and a prime's edit to the prime seed is accepted and recorded with its reason.
value.source: operator, 2026-11-25: seed templates for all of these; primes are encouraged to change them and can change their own

value.question: Who may create roles, and of which types?
value.default: Coder, reviewer and worker inside its own workstream; the prime creates the others.
value.answer: Anyone. Any seat may create a role of any type and start a seat in it; it informs the prime (operator ruling 2026-11-25: we are not the police). See PRD 007 req-07.

value.question: Is security a reviewer or a knowledge role, given that it carries open findings between reviews?
value.default: A reviewer, with its findings kept in its outputs and role memory.
value.answer: A reviewer. Compaction is optional for it, because it may need standing context (operator ruling 2026-11-25). See req-02 and req-06.
